title: múlva: In Two Weeks, In a Month

sections.title: Saying when something will happen
sections.content: múlva means "in" a certain amount of time from now. It goes right after a bare time-quantity phrase — a number plus a noun, with no suffix on either — so két hét múlva is "in two weeks" and egy hónap múlva is "in a month." Hungarian doesn't need a separate future tense for plans like this: the present tense together with a time word like múlva or jövő héten already makes clear that you're talking about the future.

items.english: We're traveling abroad in two weeks.
We're planning the trip next week.

sections.content: múlva already carries the meaning of "in," so don't add another word for it — két hét múlva, not egy -ban forma or any extra suffix on hét.
